cross_protein_control.note: If cross-protein distance is not clearly ABOVE the within-protein distance, the invariant does not discriminate folds and invariance would be worthless.

finding: Persistent homology is STABLE, not invariant. On a tight ensemble the barcodes can coincide exactly; on a disperse ensemble thermal breathing moves the filtration itself and d_B > 0. The directive's d_B == 0.000 guarantee therefore cannot be asserted as written and must be restated as a separation test with a stated tolerance.

implementation_scope.beta_1: EXACT for the complex: |E| - |V| + beta_0 - rank(boundary_2), the rank taken over GF(2) by Gaussian elimination on the 2-simplex boundary matrix. This is homology, NOT the 1-skeleton cycle-rank surrogate.
implementation_scope.curves: Betti curves over a shared epsilon grid; curve L1 is a conservative stand-in for the bottleneck distance d_B (d_B=0 implies this is 0, not conversely).
implementation_scope.dihedrals: CA-ONLY pseudo-dihedrals from consecutive C-alpha quadruples. These are NOT true (phi, psi) Ramachandran angles, which need N, CA, C. Labelled as pseudo so no reader mistakes them.
implementation_scope.grid_note: epsilon grid is coarse (8 points). A coarse grid can force spurious d_B == 0 by quantisation, which is why the cross-protein control is required before any invariance claim.

not_claims: CA-only pseudo-dihedrals are not true Ramachandran angles
curve L1 is not bottleneck distance
coarse epsilon grid can force spurious zero distances
two ensembles do not characterise the tight/disperse boundary
subsampled to at most 8 models per ensemble
what: Directive-3 persistence-invariance test on real NMR ensembles. Replaces the FALSIFIED 8 A contact map (ledger 1991) with topological invariants.
